title: Functions with No Return (Void)
story: Your smart home assistant just needs to announce things — "Dinner's ready!" or "Door is locked!" It doesn't need to calculate anything, just speak up.
why: Not every function needs to produce a value. Some functions exist purely to perform actions — print messages, log events, or trigger effects.
analogy: A void function is like a megaphone announcement — it broadcasts a message but doesn't hand you anything back.
try_it: Create a void function called `weather_report` that takes temperature (Int) and condition (Str) and prints a nicely formatted weather summary.
tips: Omit the `-> ReturnType` and the function returns nothing — it just runs its body
Void functions are all about SIDE EFFECTS — things they do to the world (printing, logging)
You can still pass parameters to void functions — they just don't produce a result
common_mistakes: Trying to assign a void function's result: `let x = announce("hi");` — there's nothing to assign
Adding `-> Unit` unnecessarily — it's the default, so you can just leave it off
Forgetting that void functions can still be useful — not every function needs to return a number
